# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 14
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 14

---

*[Paradise continues: more categories of the righteous. The place of the virgins and those who suffered.]*

1. And there were also those who had kept the virginity of their body. And they praised God with a loud voice.

2. And I saw also those who had suffered for the sake of righteousness. And they were clad in white raiment and had crowns upon their heads, and they praised God with a loud voice.

3. And I asked: "Where are those who had suffered more than these?"

4. And the angel said to me: "This is a more glorious place which God prepared for those who have kept the virginity of their body and for those who have been pure."

5. And I saw also Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and they were there in very great gladness.

6. And I saw also the angels of light and the seraphim above them, and a multitude of righteous in a great white light.

7. And I marvelled greatly and rejoiced, and I asked: "What is the place and who are these people in it?"

8. And the angel answered me: "This is a place prepared for those who have suffered for the sake of God and also for those who fear him."

9. And I, Peter, asked my Lord: "Is it not possible that sinners could receive mercy even at the last moment? For it is written that God is compassionate and merciful and does not desire the death of the sinner."

10. And the Lord said to me: "Hear me, Peter: What I have said to you before, and what you have heard and seen, that is the truth. No one sinning and dying in his sin will be saved."

11. "But there shall be mercy for some, and some shall not be saved, but they shall go to the place of punishment for ever."

12. "Those whom I have received from below shall receive mercy through me, whom I have delivered."

---
*EMET note: Verse 12 introduces a hint of intercession-from-Christ — Jesus may receive some from punishment — which is in tension with the earlier absolute statements. Some scholars see this as a later addition or textual variant.*
